items.speaker: Andrew Bailey
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, 5-4 (4 for a cut) on 2026-02-05. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: I therefore see scope for some further easing of policy. This does not mean that I expect to cut Bank Rate at any particular meeting.

items.speaker: Clare Lombardelli
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, 5-4 (4 for a cut) on 2026-02-05. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: Taken together, I prefer to hold Bank Rate at its current level. I am more concerned about the costs of cutting rates too quickly than too slowly, including the risks to credibility from any potential policy reversal that is not in response to a new shock.

items.speaker: Catherine Mann
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, 5-4 (4 for a cut) on 2026-02-05. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: A cut now would overweight the importance of the near-term mechanical disinflation and risk higher term premia.

items.speaker: Dave Ramsden
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, 5-4 (4 for a cut) on 2026-02-05. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: cut to 3.5%.
items.text: However, with my starting point for an estimate of the neutral rate of around 3%, I judge that policy should be less restrictive in order to meet the 2% target sustainably in the medium term.

items.speaker: Alan Taylor
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, 5-4 (4 for a cut) on 2026-02-05. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: cut to 3.5%.
items.text: If we expect to be at or below the target with significant slack emerging in about six months, a neutral rate of 3% should be in our sights now.

items.speaker: Andrew Bailey
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, unanimous on 2026-03-19. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: Monetary policy must, however, respond to the risk of a more persistent effect on UK CPI inflation.

items.speaker: Sarah Breeden
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, unanimous on 2026-03-19. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: Absent this shock, the underlying disinflation process had continued broadly as I expected and, consistent with my vote in February, I would have expected to vote for a cut again in March.

items.speaker: Swati Dhingra
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, unanimous on 2026-03-19. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: If we see something resembling the lower-inflation scenario, I would expect to reduce Bank Rate, possibly quickly, over the rest of the year.

items.speaker: Megan Greene
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, unanimous on 2026-03-19. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: The risk of inflation persistence has risen, perhaps significantly, in light of the negative supply shock from the war in the Middle East.

items.speaker: Clare Lombardelli
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, 7-2 (2 for a hike) on 2026-06-18. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: Were signals to indicate inflation would persist above target, this would require policy to respond more forcefully to inflationary pressures.

items.speaker: Catherine Mann
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, 7-2 (2 for a hike) on 2026-06-18. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: Research shows that a forceful Bank Rate decision can have a quick effect on inflation and inflation expectations. So I have time to continue to evaluate measures of inflation expectations and financial restrictiveness to determine whether firms’ pricing and 2027 wage negotiations are on a target-consistent path for the medium term.

items.speaker: Dave Ramsden
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, 7-2 (2 for a hike) on 2026-06-18. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: Holding Bank Rate at this meeting keeps options open as we continue to learn more about the path of the conflict. My reaction function will remain state-contingent on both the development of the conflict, and what that means for the outlook for the economy.

items.speaker: Sarah Breeden
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, 6-3 (3 for a hike) on 2026-07-30. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: Financial conditions facing households and businesses have tightened materially since the onset of the conflict, and consistent with the baseline, provide sufficient restrictiveness for now.

items.speaker: Swati Dhingra
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, 6-3 (3 for a hike) on 2026-07-30. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: An increase in Bank Rate now would be disproportionate as, unlike 2022, the starting point for this shock is much softer and the policy stance is more restrictive.

items.speaker: Megan Greene
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, 6-3 (3 for a hike) on 2026-07-30. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hike to 4%.
items.text: Unsurprisingly, there has been scant evidence of second-round effects, but I expect some to emerge.

items.speaker: Huw Pill
items.context: Policy rate 3.75%. Last decision: hold, 6-3 (3 for a hike) on 2026-07-30. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hike to 4%.
items.text: The profound uncertainty surrounding the energy price outlook is likely to be prolonged and of unknown duration, rendering efforts to fine-tune the economy with monetary policy hazardous.

items.speaker: Kazuo Ueda
items.venue: Speech at a meeting with business leaders
items.context: Policy rate 0.5%. Last decision: hold, 7-2 (2 for a hike) on 2025-09-19. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: Given these factors, it is important, first of all, to maintain accommodative financial conditions and thereby firmly support economic activity.

items.speaker: Kazuo Ueda
items.venue: Speech at a meeting with business leaders
items.context: Policy rate 0.5%. Last decision: hold, 7-2 (2 for a hike) on 2025-09-19. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: The Bank will carefully examine the likelihood that the baseline scenario for economic activity and prices will be realized, as well as both upside and downside risks, and will make monetary policy decisions as appropriate and without any preconceptions.

items.speaker: Ryozo Himino
items.venue: Speech at a meeting with local leaders
items.context: Policy rate 0.5%. Last decision: hold, unanimous on 2025-07-31. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: Therefore, if the baseline scenario described earlier is realized, it would be appropriate for the Bank to continue, in accordance with improvement in economic activity and prices, to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation (Chart 9).

items.speaker: Ryozo Himino
items.venue: Speech at a meeting with local leaders
items.context: Policy rate 0.5%. Last decision: hold, unanimous on 2025-07-31. Market-implied path: not available. Speaker's last vote: hold.
items.text: To date, we have not seen clear signs of such effects, but we cannot exclude the possibility that they could emerge in time.
